questions.q: Why do we seal the last 13 weeks of data before choosing any model?
options: It gives a final, honest score on data that played no part in choosing features or models
Thirteen weeks is too little data to matter
Sealed data trains the model faster
It lets us shuffle the remaining weeks
questions.explain: The sealed weeks are touched once at the end, so the result is not inflated by repeated tuning against it.

questions.q: Which of these is a legitimate feature for a 13-week forecast made at the start of the quarter?
options: Last week's sales for week 10 of the horizon
The planned promotion calendar
The actual sales in the sealed test weeks
The average of the next 13 weeks
questions.explain: A feature is allowed only if you would know it at forecast time. The promotion plan is known in advance; future sales are not.

questions.q: In the lesson's backtest, why was the seasonal naive forecast worse (MAE 129.0) than the naive one (95.7)?
options: It used too many weeks of history
Seasonal naive can never be beaten by naive
It copied last year's promotion spikes into weeks where promotions did not occur
The metric was calculated in the wrong units
questions.explain: Promotions in this data do not repeat on the same calendar weeks each year, so copying last year's values imports spikes in the wrong places.

options: Randomly shuffling weeks into train and test sets
Training on all the data and testing on the same data
Forecasting only the first week ever recorded
Training on data before an origin date, forecasting the next horizon, then moving the origin forward and repeating
questions.explain: It scores a model over several time-ordered windows, so one lucky split cannot decide the result.

questions.q: Why write down the success criteria (for example, beat the best baseline by at least 20%) before modeling?
options: So the bar cannot be moved after seeing the results
Because the metric has to be chosen at random
Because a model must always beat its baseline by exactly 20%
So the sealed test set can be used for tuning
questions.explain: Fixing the goal in advance keeps the evaluation honest. The 20% figure is a choice for this project, not a standard.
